177.t: Clay Giles in the brass bands, and Robichaux's bass drum
177.s: Clay played every brass band in town; John Robichaux was the first to play bass drum in the street; the uncles played only brass bands.
177.q: Well, he played with the Salsa and occasionally with Moe's, every brass band in existence because he was a good drummer and anytime they had a chance to use him they would always try to get Clay Gile. Because Old Man Robichaud was the first man I understand that I heard that played a bass drum in…

709.t: The plantation brass band: parades, size, instruments, breakup
709.s: The band paraded for the masons at Woodland and nearby. It had ten pieces: cornets, trombones, altos, baritone, bass and drums, no clarinet. It broke up as the old players died or left, and Sonny Henry is recalled.
709.ch: Early life and the plantation brass band
709.q: Yeah. I played music down there, who they are, in the parades down there. They had the mason down there. But the mason was at Woodland.

248.t: Uniformed dance bands and Hippolyte Charles's saxophone orchestra
248.s: Dawson describes the Olympia and Eureka dance bands in uniform, Hippolyte Charles's reading band with two saxes and a conservatory-trained leader, and the Blaze Away and Golden Rule bands.
248.ch: Learning, lawn parties and band rivalries
248.q: You know, uh, we had, uh, we had the Olympia, we had the Olympia band. Not no, not no, marching band. What's your name? Dancing band. They had the Eureka. That was a dance band, too? Yeah. We had the, uh, blazer way. They had, uh, uh, uh, Yeah.

249.t: Billy Marrero's father and the old Imperial band picture
249.s: An old picture of an early six-piece band, Imperial and Superior, owned by an old lady.
249.q: Listen, I know later now, listen, we'll tell you this now, between you and I, one of the oldest bands in town. You understand? They'd be surprised if you get this. Billy Moran, you know what I'm talking about? Billy Moran. Oh yes, the line's Moran's father. That's his daddy.

826.t: Playing brass bands: instruments, funerals and band arrangements
826.s: Discussion of the eleven-piece brass band, E-flat horn, funerals, and how parts were split for trumpets and trombones.
826.q: I just used this and this and condition, you see. They had music and everything for it. And it was a music band. They didn't do much. They played a little by head but most of them music, marches and all that stuff, they had heavy funerals, you tell you. They had a real number one band for eleven…

254.s: They discuss neighborhood brass bands: about twelve men, mostly marches and parades rather than jazz.
254.q: Well, the brass band, they used to, they worked with marching. The brass band. The brass band. When, uh, when you were small, they didn't, the brass band didn't play jazz too much, but they more played march? Yeah, marches and parades. Parades. Humor? Oh yeah, humor. Humor. Humor. Humor. Oh yeah,…

174.t: Best old bands, Old Man Allen, and Dejan's own brass band career
174.s: He names the best old bands, recalls playing once with Old Man Allen, then Eureka and the Young Tuxedo, while always keeping his own band.
174.q: What do you mean the old parade band? Yeah. The El Seltzer, the Hornward, the band band that the parade was leading, and the Tuxedo, you know, one Celestad. Imperial. Well yeah, Imperial, and Old Man Allen had a good band too. When you played in the Old Man Allen band you had to clean your eyes…

571.t: Reading brass bands, hunky-tunk bands and band size
571.s: George says old funeral and parade bands were reading bands, describes 'tunk bands' at the back, and gives a size of ten to twelve pieces.
571.ch: Lake boats and brass band practice
571.q: Well they had a few get together bands, they like, the Labor Day, they have so many bands that they had to send out to countries and get them, you know. Well they'd have a few get together bands that were playing this, the hit stuff like that.

734.t: Other bands and the brass band around Thibodeaux
734.s: Other local bands, the brass band his uncles played in, drummers, and why he loved Joe Gabriel.
734.q: Well no, there's a few bands there, Joe Gabriel, and uh, Claiborne William, you know? Yeah, he was in Donaldsonville. Donaldsonville, and they had a band in Crowley I think, the Bower Boys in Oregon City. I played with them too, Johnny Bower and Willie Bower and...

45.t: Onward Brass Band lineup with Manuel Perez
45.s: Williams recalls his first regular brass-band job, with the Onward Brass Band, and lists its trumpets, trombones, altos, clarinet and drummers.
45.q: My first parade band? No, I didn't play with Ridgely. My first parade band. I don't believe I can remember what band I played with first. I knew I was a member of the Onward Brass Band, Manuel Perez, you know. That was the Manuel, and you played with him? Yeah, that was the Onward Brass Band. That…

828.s: He played in Rena's unorganized ten-piece brass band and objects to saxophones in brass bands.
828.ch: Bass horn, tubas and Kid Rena
828.q: No, he never had an organized brass band. He wasn't organized. Well how many pieces did he usually use? He used to use 10. Ten.

857.t: Street parades with the Onward band and its personnel
857.s: Foster says he played parades with Tuxedo and Onward and names the Onward line-up under Manuel Perez.
857.q: Old man Barberan Alto and old man Adolph Alexander Sr. On the baritone. Yeah, baritone.

192.t: Young Tuxedo as a dance band versus brass bands; Ernest Rapanya
192.s: The Young Tuxedo was strictly a dance band; Rapanya started Frazier in brass band work.
192.q: Did you stop using the name or what happened? We just stopped using it after the band, it scattered about, you see, the members scattered about because the Young Tuxedo Band of the day, that's considered a band. That's considered a brass band, isn't it? Yeah, that's what I wondered.

176.t: De De's first brass band with Gunye
176.s: De De recalls his cousin Dejean's brass band, its members, music and marching tempos.
176.q: I don't want to start playing with the boys. Let me see where the... In the Jefferson Boys? Yeah Jefferson City Boys, I mean the bass band. Yeah, he's playing for the... I can't follow that man's name. Rene, how much? Wait a minute, I called his name this morning. Corpintuck. Wait a minute. He did,…

193.t: Funeral and brass bands: Manuel Perez, Chris Kelly, Excelsior
193.s: He played brass bands under Manuel Perez and Chris Kelly, and parades while a student of Tio.
193.q: ones yeah well i played with uh manuel perez old man joey moret played with him while chris he had a band funeral band chris kelly chris kelly had a funeral band manu perez

297.t: Brass bands: Sonny Henry, Tuxedo and Eureka
297.s: Sonny Henry played with the Tuxedo brass band; Summers played mostly mixed bands in the 1920s and brass bands like Eureka from about 1938.
297.q: With, uh, brass bands? Yeah. Tuxedo. You worked with a Tuxedo band? I played with, uh, Eureka a lot, you know. Uh-huh. Then I played with mixed bands, you know. Yeah. Like Kid Howard.

858.t: The Onward band's return and Johnson's own brass band work
858.s: Talk of the Onward band's return, then Johnson says he played with the Tuxedo brass band.
858.ch: Brass bands and the WPA band

825.t: Allen's Brass Band, the old Eureka and Big Landry's E-flat cornet
825.s: Ernie's most organized brass band was old man Allen's. He also played funerals with the old Eureka under Big Landry, who played a loud E-flat cornet to the end.
825.q: No, no, I played in the most organized band that I played in, the brass band, was with old man Allen, Red Allen's daddy. Allen's brass band.

128.t: Brass bands he played with and how they played
128.s: He names Kid Rene, Chris Kelly and Punch Miller; Buddy Petit's brass band played by head while Tuxedo and Pacific read marches.
128.q: Oh, I played with, I played with a lot of bands. One of the team and brass bands, Kid Rene, Chris Kelly, Kid Punch. Yeah, play with the, play with the record. I don't play with the exhausts, no, I don't play with them. I was playing, I didn't play good like that. Tuxedo.
